needs_human.note: With --with-drives, shared_writes drops every drive source under .r5-stack (r5_stack.py:286). The merged backend config then points only at clones, so the drive list is empty and the pre-run check no longer guards any original drive path. The only protection for a non-backend service that writes an original drive is plan_overlay's redirect.; Without --with-drives, file operations in the clone (rename, upload, move) fail as HTTP 500s. decisions.md step (5) records that the rename dialog stays open with no error message. The developer sees a raw failure, not a message that the drives are read-only.; Without --with-drives, every startup and daily purge in the clone logs one exception per expired trash row and a 'left N file(s) behind' warning, because unlink raises EROFS. This log noise is expected, but nothing in the script mentions it.

Drive detection compares strings exactly, so a drives.json path with a trailing slash or other unnormalised form does not match its bind target. That drive is then not made read-only and the check does not flag it.; The compose passthrough applies the mount check even to teardown subcommands (down, stop, rm).
